messages:
Asha: heads up — saw a spike of 429s on canary after the kernel pin change around 11:02. tail latency jumped, throughput dropped ~12%.
Micah: ugh. which kernel and which workload?
Asha: pinned to fast-attn-v2 on rtx-pool for the 13B family. KV hit rate for that test is ~22%, seq len mostly 256.
Samir: low KV hit + aggressive kernel that assumes long continuous KV use can explode token budget. any logs?
Asha: pasted excerpts: 
```
2026-01-18T11:02:11Z INFO admit: window=40ms token_budget=120 inflight=88 kv_hit_rate=0.22 kernel=fast-attn-v2
2026-01-18T11:02:11Z WARN shed: soft_reject=true policy=hard-throttle queued=140 returned=429
```
Micah: interesting — the admit controller kept target batch size high, so many requests waited for a batch that never filled because KV cache misses prevented fast continuation. result = head-of-line blocking + lease timeouts.
Yuki: that fits a pattern we saw last month. solution we tried: dynamic token_budget = base * (1 + kv_hit_rate * kv_multiplier). simple but effective.
Samir: +1. also consider kernel-pref hints on batch formation: if a request has recent KV hits, prefer grouping with similar ones; otherwise favor fast-small-batch kernel that avoids long assembly waits.
Asha: can we try two quick probes on canary? 1) adaptive-token-budget with kv multiplier 0.8, 2) bias batch sampler toward low-wait (max-wait 15ms) for requests with kv_hit_rate<0.4.
Micah: I'll spin canary flags. config snippet: 
```
admit_controller:
  token_budget_base: 100
  kv_multiplier: 0.8
  max_batch_wait_ms: 15
  sampler:
    prefer_low_wait_for_kv_miss: true
```
Micah: also enabling per-request kernel_hint: fallback_kernel=small-latency if sampler sees >30% misses in last 10s.
Yuki: beware the regression we saw where fallback_kernel caused oscillation — the kernel handoff was too aggressive and warmed different kernels repeatedly. add a sticky cooldown: kernel_hint_ttl=30s.
Samir: good catch. add hysteresis on admit: once we lower budget for a lane, gradually ramp back over 60s to avoid oscillations.
Asha: perf-bot just posted a quick profile from the canary run (first probe, 5m): 
perf-bot: 2026-01-18T11:08 profile summary: p50=18ms p95=220ms p99=730ms 429_rate=3.2% CPU-steal negligible KV-cache-miss=78%
Micah: 78% miss — that explains it. we'll flip probe 2 now (low-wait bias + kernel cooldown).
Asha: can we also add a lightweight sampling hook to tag requests that pay the cost of a big batch vs small kernel? just a counter to measure economics.
Samir: yes — add token_cost_accounting per-request and aggregate per-tenant. quick calc will tell us when batching actually reduces unit-cost vs raises tail latency.
Yuki: I'll prepare a short postmortem template if the second probe shows regressions, but hope we can stabilize with the policy changes.
Micah: rolling probe 2 at t=11:12. will watch error budget and p99.
Asha: thx. ping me if 429s exceed 1% or p99 >500ms. :pray:
perf-bot: probe-2-started t=1766666792
Micah: early numbers after 90s: 429_rate=0.6% p99=420ms kv_miss=65% throughput +4%
Asha: looks promising. leave for 10m then decide on gradual rollout.
Samir: follow-up action items: 1) add kernel_hint_ttl and admit hysteresis (owner: Samir), 2) add token_cost_accounting metric (owner: Micah), 3) run 30m canary with mixed real traffic (owner: Yuki).
Yuki: will do. posting notes to the eng-runtime runbook after the canary completes.
Micah: if this stabilizes we should update the kernel selection doc to include kv-hit-aware batching heuristics.
Asha: agreed. thanks everyone.
